task: Rewrite a weak CV bullet into a strong, impact-first, quantified bullet point suitable for a PM or tech role application
scoring_calibration: Be strict. Reserve 9-10 only for bullets that would make a senior recruiter or hiring manager stop and take notice. A bullet with no metric scores max 6. Most rewrites should score 5-7. Generic rewrites that just add action verbs without substance score 1-4.

dimensions.name: impact_first
dimensions.description: Does the bullet lead with the outcome or result, not the activity? Bullets starting with 'Responsible for', 'Worked on', 'Helped with', or 'Managed' score 1-3. Bullets that bury the result at the end score 4-6. Bullets where the first 4 words communicate the value delivered score 8-10.

scoring_guide.1-3: Starts with activity or responsibility. 'Managed a team of engineers to build a feature.'
scoring_guide.4-6: Has impact but it's buried. 'Led cross-functional team to ship onboarding flow, improving activation by 22%.'
scoring_guide.7-8: Impact comes early but not in the very first words.
scoring_guide.9-10: First 4 words communicate the value. 'Increased activation 22% by shipping a redesigned onboarding flow with a 6-person team.'

dimensions.name: quantified
dimensions.description: Does the bullet include at least one specific metric — a number, percentage, dollar amount, time saved, or scale indicator? Vague words like 'significantly', 'greatly', 'substantially' score 1-3. A single concrete number scores 7-8. Multiple metrics or a metric with context (baseline + improvement) scores 9-10.

scoring_guide.1-3: No metric at all, or uses vague qualifiers like 'significantly improved'.
scoring_guide.4-6: Has a metric but it's weak context — e.g. team size only, or a time duration with no outcome.
scoring_guide.7-8: One clear metric — percentage, revenue, users, time saved.
scoring_guide.9-10: Two metrics OR one metric with baseline context. '34% reduction (from 8min to 5min)'.

dimensions.name: specificity
dimensions.description: Does the bullet name specific tools, methods, teams, or decisions? Generic verbs like 'leveraged', 'utilised', 'facilitated' with no object score 1-3. Named technologies, frameworks, team structures, or methodologies score 8-10.

scoring_guide.1-3: Only generic verbs. 'Leveraged data to improve the product experience.'
scoring_guide.4-6: Some specificity but still vague. 'Used analytics tools to track user behaviour.'
scoring_guide.7-8: Names one specific thing — a tool, a team, or a method.
scoring_guide.9-10: Names multiple specifics or one highly specific technical/methodological detail. 'Used Mixpanel funnel analysis to identify drop-off at step 3 of checkout.'

dimensions.name: conciseness
dimensions.description: Is the bullet under 20 words? Does every word earn its place? Filler phrases like 'in order to', 'as a result of', 'with the goal of', 'responsible for ensuring' score 1-3. Clean, tight bullets under 20 words score 9-10.

scoring_guide.1-3: Over 30 words or contains multiple filler phrases.
scoring_guide.9-10: Under 20 words. Every word is load-bearing. No filler.
